error_id: # The error account (framework 1.1.0). One row per error that was found — or that is
# known to be there and was never caught.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#   The provenance ledger records what ran. The claim ledger records what was concluded.
#   Neither records what went wrong. In agent-assisted analysis that omission is
#   load-bearing: the failure mode is not a crash but a plausible wrong answer, and the
#   errors that produce it are mostly not the ones a human analyst would make.
# class — three values, and the difference between them is the point:
#   inherited  the error was there before the agent touched anything: a swapped sample,
#              an incompatible genome build, a confounding batch. A careful analyst
#              working by hand hits these too.
#   amplified  the workflow made an inherited error faster, larger or quieter. Choosing
#              the wrong genome build near the start can travel all the way into a
#              figure and a manuscript without any independent check firing.
#   emergent   the failure is produced by the agent's own mechanics. These have no
#              hand-analysis equivalent, which is why they are easy to miss and why
#              `emergent_kind` is required:
#                goal_drift                 iterative planning quietly replaces the
#                                           question asked with an easier one to answer
#                context_loss               pairing, exclusion criteria or a negative
#                                           control drop out of the working context
#                stale_memory               a remembered fact is used past its expiry
#                retrieval_poisoning        instructions found in a repository or in
#                                           metadata are obeyed as instructions
#                incomplete_tool_description  the tool does less than its description says
# detected_by : auto | human | not_detected
#   `not_detected` is not a shrug. It records an error you believe is present but that
#   no check caught — the honest form of "we cannot rule this out". It then REQUIRES
#   containment=uncontained and an empty detected_at: something that was never detected
#   cannot have been contained on a date.
# detected_at : ISO-8601 date. Empty when detected_by=not_detected.
# containment : where it was fixed (a script, a re-run, a design change). `uncontained`
#   when the error is still live. Uncontained errors must appear in the deliverable's
#   unverified declaration.
# propagated_to : comma-separated claim_ids this error reaches. Each must exist in
#   claim-ledger.tsv — an error that reached a claim nobody recorded is a lost trail.
#   Write `-` when it reached no claim.
# NO-ERRORS DECLARATION
#   An empty ledger is indistinguishable from a ledger nobody filled in, so "we looked
#   and found nothing" has to be said out loud, with the check that supports it:
#       # none-detected-by: <the check you actually ran>
#   That declaration is required whenever this file has no data rows, and rejected when
#   it is blank or a placeholder. If any step is recorded `deviated` in
#   provenance-ledger.tsv, this file must have at least one row and the declaration does
#   not substitute for it.
# none-detected-by: UNKNOWN
